Maia for Inventory exception reports

Review stock exceptions with the timestamp attached.

Maia applies approved thresholds to an inventory snapshot and demand inputs. The inventory owner sees what needs review without an availability guarantee.

All use cases ↗

Start with a snapshot

Provide an inventory snapshot, its timestamp, approved thresholds, demand inputs, and product mappings. State whether quantities represent available, on-hand, reserved, or inbound stock.

Ask Maia to retain those definitions beside the results. A quantity without its state can lead to the wrong action.

Build the exception list

Maia can apply the supplied thresholds, group exceptions by warehouse or owner, and flag stale snapshots. It can identify missing mappings and unusual changes for investigation.

The report should not promise availability or recommend a purchase without the owner's review.

Include inbound quantities only when their expected dates and confidence are part of the source. A purchase order does not mean stock is available. Show inbound supply separately.

Review in the operations channel

The inventory owner checks freshness, thresholds, inbound timing, and known promotions. Other teams can add relevant context, such as a delayed shipment or revised campaign date.

A practical example

Three products fall below the approved two-week threshold. Maia notes that the west warehouse snapshot is six hours older and one product has inbound stock not yet received. It separates that case instead of treating every low quantity alike.

The inventory owner verifies the inbound date and decides which item needs purchasing review.

Connect the next decision

The report can feed a promotion readiness review or an order exception discussion. Keep the source timestamp attached when the information moves between channels. A newer snapshot may change the conclusion.

Record the owner's disposition for each exception, such as monitor, expedite, transfer, or investigate. These labels support the next review without authorizing the underlying action.

Review thresholds after a promotion, supplier change, or seasonal shift. Keep the old rule with its effective dates so later reports do not compare exceptions created under different policies as though they were alike.

Include the units for every threshold and quantity. Cases, items, and selling units can produce different conclusions from the same number.

Common questions

Can Maia place a purchase order?

This workflow prepares exceptions. Purchasing requires a separately verified action and the authorized owner's approval.

Does the report show live availability?

It shows the supplied or connected snapshot and its timestamp. Do not present it as live unless the source and refresh behavior prove that.

How are thresholds chosen?

The business owner supplies them. Maia applies and explains the rule but should not invent safety stock policy.
